purpose: Independent source collation of Turner's three elemental triplicity classifications

source.title: Henry Cornelius Agrippa, His Fourth Book of Occult Philosophy: Of Geomancy
source.witness: Robert Turner English translation, London 1655; printed by J.C. for John Harrison
source.chronology: The web page identifies the text as a 1655 English translation and attributes the Fourth Book to Agrippa. This is a late witness for this project, not certification of the early Cod. Sang. 756 program.

source_sections.intro: The page first describes sixteen figures and their planetary and zodiacal associations.
source_sections.classification_A: The paragraph beginning 'And these are the infallible comparisons...' gives a sign/course-based triplicity order.
source_sections.classification_B: The following paragraph beginning 'But if any one will constitute these triplicities according to the nature of the Planets...' gives the author's preferred planetary/figure order.
source_sections.classification_C: The next paragraph beginning 'This order is also far more true...' records the vulgar order as an alternative.
source_sections.preferred_note: Turner says the planetary/figure order is rather to be observed than the first, and calls it more true and rational than the vulgar order.

frozen_figure_bits.convention: single=1, double=0, top-to-bottom; integer most significant bit top

A_sign_course.source_paraphrase: The first triplicity list follows the order and manner of the zodiacal signs.

Amissio.reason: Amitia is the source spelling; likely Amissio but not silently normalized

spelling_options.lower_literal: Treat Amitia as an unnormalized source token: Amissio has no assigned element in this printed list, so the list is not a complete canonical 16-figure table.
spelling_options.upper_emendation: Treat Amitia as a probable spelling error for Amissio: Amissio is air and all 16 frozen canonical figures receive an assignment.

B_planetary_preferred.source_paraphrase: The author reorganizes the triplicities by the natures of the planets and figures, then explicitly prefers this order to the first.

C_vulgar.source_paraphrase: The page then reports a commonly used alternative order, explicitly contrasting it with the preferred planetary/figure order.

limits: The source tables are classifications in one 1655 witness, not an independent Voynich meaning or early-source confirmation.
Amitia is retained as printed in classification A; the Amissio mapping is an explicit upper/emendation option only.
No target labels, target scoring, or additional manuscript access was used.
